query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and is intended to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance in its solidified solid-solution state, but its dynamic behavior across different temperatures and strain rates lacks a theoretical explanation. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could account for this behavior, and what controlled comparison within that regime would distinguish it? Specify predictions relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and a falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The enhanced strength–ductility balance in the Co‐free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is due to a temperature- and strain rate–dependent modulation of dislocation mobility. Removing Co alters the lattice distortion and effective stacking fault energy such that, under certain thermal and loading conditions, mobile dislocations periodically lock and unlock via interactions with the local solute atmospheres. This behavior—analogous to dynamic strain aging—delays flow localization and permits sustained plasticity.
generation.material_initial_state: A as-cast, single-phase solid-solution Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy produced under conventional casting conditions.
generation.intervention: Perform tensile tests across a range of temperatures and strain rates on the Co-free alloy and compare with the equiatomic Co-containing (CoCrFeMnNi) alloy.
generation.conditions: Tests performed from room temperature to moderately high temperatures (e.g., up to 600 K) and spanning strain rates from quasi-static (~10⁻³ s⁻¹) to high strain rate (~10³ s⁻¹) under controlled tensile loading.
generation.structural_mediator: Dynamic dislocation structures mediated by altered local lattice distortions and solute-dislocation (Cottrell-type) interactions, influenced by an effectively modified stacking fault energy.
generation.mechanism: The removal of Co changes the local chemical environment and lattice distortion, which in turn alters the activation barrier for dislocation glide. Under intermediate temperatures and variable strain rates, these changes lead to periodic dislocation locking and unlocking. This mechanism delays strain localization and enhances work hardening, sustaining ductility while elevating dynamic strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the equiatomic alloy baseline, the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy should exhibit higher strain rate sensitivity, evidenced by pronounced serrated flow (indicative of dynamic dislocation locking/unlocking) in the stress–strain curves at intermediate temperatures. This should correlate with a measurable delay in the onset of plastic instability while preserving or improving ductility.
generation.baseline: Mechanical performance metrics (e.g., yield strength, strain hardening rate, strain rate sensitivity) of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA under identical testing conditions.
generation.boundary: This mechanistic behavior is expected only within the tested regime (room temperature to ~600 K and strain rates spanning ~10⁻³ to 10³ s⁻¹); outside these conditions other mechanisms (such as low-temperature twinning or high-temperature phase instabilities) may dominate.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative influence of altered solute-dislocation interactions due to Co removal and the exact role of stacking fault energy variations are not fully established and will require further detailed study; alternative mechanisms (e.g., nanoscale twinning) might also contribute.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the Co-free FeNiCrMn HEA and another set of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. Conduct tensile experiments over a temperature range from room temperature to 600 K and strain rates ranging from 10⁻³ to 10³ s⁻¹. Simultaneously record high-resolution stress–strain curves to capture serrated flow and perform post-deformation TEM/EBSD analysis to assess dislocation structures and evidence of solute atmospheres.
measurements: Stress–strain curves to determine yield strength, strain hardening rate, and strain rate sensitivity
Identification and statistical analysis of serration events during deformation
TEM/EBSD characterization of dislocation arrangements and potential Cottrell atmospheres
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Co-free alloy does not show a statistically significant difference in strain rate sensitivity and serrated flow behavior compared to the equiatomic alloy, or if microstructural analysis fails to reveal differences in dislocation locking/unlocking or solute atmospheres, then the hypothesis that dynamic dislocation interactions govern the observed dynamic behavior is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Overall, this comprehensive study provides evidence for the unique elastic and plastic deformation behavior of the single BCC solid-solution phase refractory HEA at elevated temperatures using in situ neutron experiments coupled with theoretical calculations. The results of the ND and characterization of the microstructure show the excellent BCC single-phase stability up to 900°C. Furthermore, the present alloy has the high yield strength and excellent plasticity at RT and softening resistance at elevated temperatures. The lattice strain evolution results show the distinctive elastic deformation behavior as an elastic isotropy at RT and less temperature dependency in the elastic anisotropic deformation behavior than conventional metallic materials at elevated temperatures. The single-crystal elastic moduli are obtained from the in situ ND data coupled with the Kroner model approach, showing excellent agreement with the experimental values determined from RUS measurements and first-principles calculations. Hence, it is vital to comprehend the dynamic behavior of as-cast NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy under low/high-speed loading and expand its applications. Many researchers were devoted to investigating the deformation behavior of the high-entropy alloy at different strain rate levels (1 × 10−8 s−1 to 10 s−1) []. From the recent research, serration behavior was found in the high-entropy alloy CoCrFeMnNi prepared by powder metallurgy at a low strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1 and the high strain rates (1 × 103 s−1 to 3 × 103 s−1) []. Serration behavior was supposed to be associated with Cottrell atmosphere interaction with moving dislocations, slip bands, and dynamic strain aging, i.e., the dynamic breakaway/locking of dislocations from/by mobile solute atoms at intermediate temperatures. Until now, only several researches on dynamic behavior of high-entropy alloys under high strain rates (beyond 1 × 103 s−1) have been published. Kumar et al.
